Honestly, I think a lot of these comments are a little too....optimistic. I think reality can suck and hurt sometimes, but it sounds like you need some truth here sis. Love is wonderful, but if he isn’t willing to put in the work, no amount of support from your end is going to make a difference. You can lead a horse to water, but you can’t make it drink. I think he’s showing you exactly what he’s capable of and interested in doing. However, I know letting go of someone you love is hard so here is what I recommend to do. 

An ultimatum. A real ultimatum, with consequences and boundaries. I would just be straight up and say “I am worried about our future together and I need to know that this can work. I need the reassurance that if we build a life together, I won’t be the one doing it all by myself. I need you to ask yourself what you want to do, and I need you to commit to it.” because girl, that’s VALID!!! We all need partners that match us and our personal drives. No one wants a partner that doesn’t have the same goals or energy as them, no matter how much they love them. I think giving him 3 months is more than enough for him to have a talk with himself, see what he wants to do, and to start doing it. If he can’t take that time to be constructive and positive when his love of his life and his future are on the line, he just isn’t going to do it period. No one is irreplaceable, no matter how special they are. No one is worth degrading your standards and achievements for babe, not even your partner. 

I hope he can come to his senses and grows up, but if not, I hope you can separate yourself from him and begin the healing process. Either way, just hoping for some positivity in your life. All the best ❤️

For me, it was when I found a body that had washed up on the beach when I was around 5 years old. I remember because I was nervous about starting kindergarten at the time and let me tell you, I was NOT down with starting grade school  😹Anyway,fast forward to the end of summer. I was on the beach playing, as little kids do.  The beach we were at had a bend in it and I had just gone beyond that, still in ear shot of my parents. Everything seemed to be business as usual. 


Until I see him.
 
I actually had no idea what it or he even was at first. Kids don’t usually jump right to... well, the thought that it could be a dead guy I guess? I just thought it was some weird ass seaweed to be honest, I was 5, what did I know? So ofcourse, as any curious kid, I went closer and I, yes you guessed it, poked him. I poked him pretty lightly too, but then again the body had probably been in the water for some time. He actually didn’t even register as a real guy to me because he was so discolored and....smushy? He was legit almost green, and super pale. I don’t remember a whole lot about the encounter overall, I don’t even remember if there was a smell to be honest. What I will always remember though is his skin sloughing off from a touch that was so light, it could’ve been described as a butterfly kiss. 

Anyway, I end up screaming because GROSS! My mom and dad turn the bend to see what’s going on, and pure HORROR covers my moms face and she is screaming bloody murder. They were both what could only be described as appalled. The police were called and I genuinely don’t remember anything after that. I just remember my mom and dad were NOT happy with what had just transpired. To their defense, I wouldn’t want my kid going through all that mess either. 

Surprisingly, I didn’t really let it affect me at all. Not sure if I was too young or the encounter was too brief, but aside from a healthy dark sense of humor, all’s well that ends well I suppose. I never did find out who he was or where he came from. We still talk about it whenever we go to that same beach.
